description: The deterministic agent integration recipe: the exact step sequence a coding agent follows to integrate Zeck from files alone — no maintainer chat, no prose-only critical instructions. Every step names the artifact that satisfies it. Validated (file existence + step coverage) by tests/unit/developer-docs/machine-schemas.test.ts.

prerequisites.runtime: Bun (the repository's package manager and runtime)
prerequisites.credentials: Three environment values from the target deployment's operator/console: ZECK_API_URL, ZECK_TOKEN (a Zeck transport credential), ZECK_APPLICATION_ID. No provider API key is ever needed client-side.

steps.action: Read the ONE canonical wire contract and the SDK (the public developer contract).

Understand the execution-centric conceptual model: Execution is THE primitive; policy precedes dispatch; capabilities are resolved before any route; budgets bound spend; sandbox isolates; verification produces evidence.
Obtain the three connection values and export them (environment only — never flags, never files).
steps.verify: All three variables set; ZECK_TOKEN is a Zeck credential, not a provider key.

steps.action: Run the quickstart end-to-end: create the SDK client, submit an idempotent execution, poll to terminal, retrieve result/evidence/cost.
steps.verify: The receipt, terminal status, result package, events and verification are printed; the replay shows replayed=true.

steps.action: Pick the workload family example matching your task; copy it. Provider-gated families print their recorded availability boundary.
Adopt the error taxonomy + idempotency discipline: retry only retryable failures, same idempotency key, fail fast on 4xx.
If you need push delivery: deploy the signature-verifying, idempotent receiver pattern.
Run the documentation battery (link checks, schema-vs-wire reconciliation, end-to-end example runs, secret scans).
steps.verify: bun run typecheck && bun run test:unit -- tests/unit/developer-docs

steps.action: When moving beyond sandbox: follow the promotion ladder, secret management and quota guidance (cross-linked to the deployment surfaces); to run a deployment yourself, follow the self-host handoff guide.

invariants: Execution is the only public primitive — there is no model-call or provider-call route.
Provider selection is forbidden in create requests (closed contracts; unknown keys rejected fail-closed).
Money is integer micro-USD strings; floats never cross.
Every POST carries an Idempotency-Key; every scoped read/command carries X-Zeck-Application.
No secret value appears in any example, doc or machine artifact (names only).
Availability is disclosed honestly: runnable vs provider-gated, with NOT RUN boundaries recorded.
